Juliaca serves as an air gateway to the Puno region and Lake Titicaca. From the city, travelers continue overland toward routes around the lake. It is an important transport hub in highland Peru, where an air journey gives way to exploring the Andean landscape.

A stop in the city complements trips to the Uros and Taquile islands. After arrival, a different side of Peru comes into view: broad mountain landscapes and small settlements along the road. Juliaca connects the capital and other parts of Peru with the lake and the lives of its lakeside communities.

Kabah is one of the archaeological sites of the Puuc region on the Yucatán Peninsula. Its best-known features include a stone arch and the Temple of the Masks, with numerous representations of the rain god Chaac. The decoration reveals architectural techniques shared by several ancient cities in this part of Mexico.

Kabah is often visited together with Uxmal. One complex is striking for its spacious plazas and buildings; at the other, the details of the facades stand out. Exploring the arch and stone structures helps visitors understand the connections among Maya settlements and see how carved imagery became part of monumental architecture.

## Cabo San Lucas: A Mexican Paradise!

## A Taste of Paradise in Cabo San Lucas!

Its remote setting and unspoiled beauty make this town a wonderful place for a peaceful escape. A string of first-class hotels lines the coast. The streets are lively both day and night. There are activities and ways to relax to suit every taste. Outdoor options include snorkeling, diving, surfing, and kayaking on the open sea. You can also go sport fishing or watch whales.

## Cajamarca: Peru's Green Jewel!

## Cajamarca: A Cradle of Inca Culture!

Cajamarca is the most important city in the mountainous north of Peru. This area was a center of pre-Inca culture and, during the Inca Empire, a major administrative center and a place where the ruler came to rest. The city is also home to the Baños del Inca, or Inca Baths, hot springs, famous throughout Peru. Their mineral-rich waters reach a temperature of +70 degrees. The city has many fascinating archaeological monuments.
